caption: @safishamsii's graphify just crossed 76,000 stars. It maps your codebase into a real graph you can query, so instead of grepping you ask and get back an actual path. Parsed locally with tree-sitter, every edge marked extracted or inferred.
capability_fact: maps your codebase into a real graph you can query
differentiator: graphify parses your code into a real graph you traverse, so you ask a plain question and get back an actual path instead of vector-search guesses.
first_reply: The repo, MIT and pip-installable with graphifyy. https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify
why_this_one: Safi came out of medical knowledge-graph research in Birmingham, carried the graph-over-embeddings idea into dev tooling, and rode it into YC S26 as a solo founder. The conviction is earned, not a pitch.

linkedin_caption: Most code tools throw your repo into a vector store and hope semantic search finds the right chunk. graphify does the opposite. It parses your code locally with tree-sitter and builds an actual graph you can walk. So you ask what connects auth to the database and it hands back a real path instead of 200 grep hits. Every edge is tagged extracted or inferred so you know what it read and what it guessed. Safi Shamsi shipped it as a skill any coding agent can install and it just crossed 76k stars. I have wanted this exact thing every time an agent grepped the same file five times.
